title: Burmese 1
college: ANU College of Asia and the Pacific
description:
Burmese is the official language of Myanmar and serves as the main lingua franca in the country as well as in Burmese communities worldwide. Myanmar embraces many ethnic groups and a diversity of cultures while being predominantly a Buddhist country. Burmese has a long history of use in literary works and music, and today the language serves as a key medium connecting Myanmar communities domestically and internationally via the internet. Students will develop an understanding of basic cultural practices in Myanmar society through this course.

In this course, students will be introduced to spoken-style Burmese language and gain communicative competence at an introductory level. The course emphasizes conversations in everyday situations such as greetings, shopping, family gatherings, describing hobbies, expressing likes and dislikes, and making reservations. Students will also learn how to use the language appropriately in different social situations while familiarizing themselves with reading and writing Burmese script.

Students will study short conversations and texts, learning the main aspects of phonology, pronunciation, grammar, and vocabulary of Burmese. Students are given opportunities to practice their Burmese listening, speaking, writing, reading, and translation skills

Throughout the semester, students will role-play conversations and occasionally interact with Burmese guest speakers who share their lived experiences of their own places and cultures to enhance students' receptive, interactive, and productive skills.
requisiteText: Students with previous experience of the language must sit a language proficiency assessment.

title: Burmese 2
college: ANU College of Asia and the Pacific
description:
This course builds on the skills acquired in Burmese 1001 and continues the study of spoken-style Burmese in both oral and written forms. Students will expand their vocabulary, develop greater grammatical accuracy, and learn to express abilities, experiences, and comparisons. Instruction emphasizes both language skills and socio-cultural awareness, enabling students to engage with everyday conversations and read simple passages in Burmese script.

Course topics include the education system, part-time job interviews, Myanmar’s geography and ethnic diversity, traditional festivals, and the contrasts between urban and rural life. Authentic materials and cultural content provide meaningful contexts for communication, while guest speakers—Burmese native speakers and Myanmar specialists—offer students exposure to authentic language and cultural perspectives.

By the end of the course, students will have strengthened their receptive, interactive, and productive skills, gaining greater confidence in both spoken and written Burmese.
requisiteText: To enrol in this course you must have completed BURM1002, undertake a Burmese language proficiency assessment or be given permission by the course convener.

title: Burmese 3
college: ANU College of Asia and the Pacific
description:
This course builds upon the skills and knowledge achieved in Burmese 1001 and 1002. Students will expand their knowledge of spoken-style Burmese and master most of its grammatical expressions. Upon completion of the course, students will gain more sophisticated spoken and written language skills.

In this course, students will delve deeper into Myanmar's traditional and changing lifestyles in recent years, including activities at weddings, funerals, and seasonal festivities. Folktales, stories of Buddha's life, and Buddhist-related rituals such as ordinations as novices and meditation practices are also included in the course. Students will be able to express both appreciation and offer insightful discussion about Myanmar's traditional culture.

By the end of the course, students will have learned vocabulary related to the topics above, new spoken-style grammar, and expressions. Students will use different registers for formal and informal language and learn more advanced communication skills for situations at university and in the workplace.

The course regularly invites Burmese native speakers and Myanmar specialists as guests to enhance students' speaking abilities and exposure to the language. Students will be encouraged to make short presentations on the topics learned to the guests. Through these interactions, students will improve their Burmese receptive, interactive, and productive skills.
requisiteText: To enrol in this course you must have completed BURM1003, undertake a Burmese language proficiency assessment or be given permission by the course convener.

title: Burmese 4
college: ANU College of Asia and the Pacific
description:
This course builds on skills learned in Burmese 3 and provides students with extensive opportunities to review, practice, and expand their knowledge of spoken-style Burmese.

The course content enables students to access authentic Burmese materials across both print and online platforms, including newspapers, magazine articles, governmental documents, short stories, poems, and excerpts from literary works. A rich variety of listening comprehension materials, including news, podcasts, and engaging discussions on academic topics, will enhance the development of students' speaking skills.

Fascinating topics include Myanmar history, economics, anthropology, mythology, and practical conversations such as negotiations and problem-solving in business/academic contexts. These diverse topics significantly deepen students' understanding of Myanmar culture and society. Students will create Burmese compositions and speech scripts in spoken-style Burmese on both assigned topics and self-selected research topics of their interest related to Myanmar.

The course regularly features Burmese native speakers and Myanmar specialists as guest speakers to enhance students' speaking abilities and provide authentic language exposure. Students will deliver presentations to these guests based on the topics covered throughout the course, creating valuable real-world communication experiences.
requisiteText: To enrol in this course you must have completed BURM2001, undertake a Burmese language proficiency assessment or be given permission by the course convener.
